content.title: About
content.content: Shark is a marine predatory fish found in oceans worldwide. Shark meat is valued for its firm texture, mild flavor, and high protein content. It is commonly used in sushi, grilling, soups, and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: There are over 500 shark species, ranging from tiny dwarf lanternsharks to massive whale sharks.
Most sharks have multiple rows of teeth that are continuously replaced throughout their lives.
Some shark species can detect the electric fields generated by the movement of their prey.
Shark meat contains low to moderate levels of mercury, so moderate consumption is advised.
In several cultures, shark meat is considered a delicacy and featured in traditional dishes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Shark meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other seafoods, shark has relatively low saturated fat content.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: It contains EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shark meat supplies B12, B6, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a source of selenium, zinc, and iron, nutrients that aid immunity and blood formation.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Meat from large predatory sharks may contain higher mercury levels; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including shark.

items.title: Texture
items.content: If not cooked properly, shark meat can be tough, increasing the risk of choking or esophageal injury.

items.title: Parasites
items.content: Like other fish, shark can harbor parasites; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shark meat can be grilled, baked, stewed, or used in sushi and sashimi after proper freezing. Marinating in lemon juice or vinegar before cooking helps tenderize the flesh.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shark in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw completely in the refrigerator before use.
